items.title: Jack DeJohnette — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: The Pat Metheny Quintet with Dewey Redman, Michael Brecker, Metheny, Charlie Haden and yourself... Pat and I had been playing together.

ctx.x: Well, not too surprising because we’re going to see that they keep their eye on you and you ultimately… Well we won’t expose the surprise. So, here’s something that I wasn’t aware of, and again, later this year, very prolific year, 2005, you release Hybrids.

That’s a project involved with my son-in-law Ben Surman, who is actually the son of the great English saxophonist/composer and also was involved in electronics too, John Surman. Ben is married to my daughter Minya and he’s also a musician and also a fine sound engineer, also does a lot of remixing, and plays electronic wind instruments as well. He’s just a wonderful human being and great artist. He took some of the recordings that we had done and remixed them, and remixed them in a way that I’ve never heard…

Metheny listened to it and really, really loved it. It’s really artistic, very thoughtful, very rhythmic. He likes drums so he hears rhythmically, very rhythmically astute. He remixed these and we even had some videos from some of the remixes. It’s brilliant what he did.
